samples.summary: Evidence-rebuild budget accounting can push the rendered region well past `maxChars`, because blocking one-liners after the first evidence fold are appended unconditionally.
samples.evidence: In the rebuild branch (lines 253-266) `used` only accounts for what has ALREADY been emitted: `if (evid && used + head.length + evid.length <= budget)`. The heads of the *remaining* `shown` findings are then appended unconditionally (`rebuilt += head; used += head.length`) with no budget test. So an early finding's evidence may consume the space reserved for later heads. Worst case: first pass fits preamble P + heading H + all heads S within `budget` B (so S ≤ B − P − H); the rebuild may then add up to ~B−P−H of evidence for finding 0 and still append the remaining ~S of heads, giving a total up to ~2B − P − H — roughly double `maxChars`. With the default 60000 that is ~120k, above GitHub's 65536 cap, so the only thing preventing a 422 is the workflow's blunt `body.slice(0, 64900)` backstop, which will cut mid-`<details>`/mid-fold. The module's stated invariant ("enforcing it over EVERYTHING", line 244) and the test at review-comment.test.mjs:158 (`out.length <= 1200`) do not cover this shape — that test uses 6 short heads with 5000-char evidence, where no evidence fits at all. A case with many heads nearly filling the budget plus one modest evidence blob reproduces the overflow.

samples.summary: The verdict header is fail-OPEN where the workflow's previous inline computation was fail-closed: a lens whose conclusion is missing/undefined now renders 🟢 "looks good".
samples.evidence: New: `l.gating !== false && l.applicable !== false && l.conclusion && l.conclusion !== "success"` — the added `l.conclusion &&` truthiness clause means `undefined`/`null`/`""` conclusion → NOT blocked. Old inline code (agent-review-on-demand.yml:543-544) did `const conclusion = p ? p.conclusion : 'failure'; if (blocking && applicable && conclusion !== 'success') blocked = true;` — an undefined conclusion counted as blocked. Combined with `collectLenses` (line 313) `conclusion: p.conclusion ?? (v ? v.conclusion : "failure")`, a lens present in panel.json (or a verdict.json) with no `conclusion` field yields a 🟢 header printed directly above a populated "🚫 Blocking (N)" section — a self-contradicting verdict. Requires malformed/older panel or verdict data, hence low confidence, but the safety direction was inverted for free.

samples.summary: `bucketOf` ignores the lens's `gating` flag, so a non-gating (advisory) lens's critical/major findings render under "🚫 Blocking" and in the blocking headline count even though they gate nothing.
samples.evidence: `bucketOf` keys only off `lane` and `normalizeSeverity(severity)`. review-panel.mjs:2562-2566 writes an advisory lens's verdict with `conclusion: "success"` and renders its summary.md with `advisory: true`, which severity.mjs:144 prints as "advisory — not gating … informational only" precisely so a green check doesn't open with a ❌. The new region has no such distinction: the `gating` field collectLenses computes (line 311) is used only for the header, so an advisory lens produces "### 🟢 Review panel: looks good" immediately followed by "#### 🚫 Blocking (N)". Latent today (all six entries in lenses.json are `"gating": "blocking"`), but the input contract documented at line 130 advertises `gating (bool)` and the renderer silently drops it.

samples.summary: `mergedFrom` ("also reported as") is rendered only for blocking findings; the merged wordings of minor/nit and relocated findings are dropped from the comment, contrary to the module's own "never silently dropped" claim.
samples.evidence: `mergedNote` is called only from `blockingEvidence` (line 99). `minorRow` (line 105) and `relocatedRow` (line 116) never call it. severity.mjs::section (lines 75-79) emitted the `also reported as` fold for EVERY severity, so for the on-demand comment this change loses the audit trail for clustered minor/nit findings, while the comment at line 69-71 asserts merged wordings are "shown on expand … (never silently dropped)".

samples.summary: Dropped reviewer-notes prose is counted as 0 hidden items, so it can be removed for length with no notice at all; and one oversized block suppresses every later block even when they would fit.
samples.evidence: The notes block is pushed with `count: 0` (line 224). In the fit loop (lines 270-279), once a block does not fit, `stopped = true` and all remaining blocks are skipped, adding only their `count` to `hiddenOptional`. If the only skipped block is the notes block, `hidden === 0` and the `… hidden for length` notice at line 283 is never emitted — the reviewer prose vanishes with no indication. The `stopped` latch also means a small "📦 Relocated" or notes block is dropped whenever a large per-lens minor/nit block preceded it, even with budget remaining.

samples.summary: Blocking sort comparator can return NaN (undefined lens-order lookup), which makes the ordering implementation-defined.
samples.evidence: `lensOrder` is keyed by `l.title || l.id` (line 193) while findings are tagged `f._lens = l.title || l.id || "lens"` (line 148). When a lens object has neither title nor id, the map key is `undefined` and the tag is `"lens"`, so `lensOrder.get(a.f._lens) - lensOrder.get(b.f._lens)` is `NaN` and the comparator becomes inconsistent (V8 then keeps arbitrary order). Duplicate titles across lenses also collapse to one index. Not reachable via `collectLenses` (title always falls back to id), but `renderReviewComment` is exported and directly callable.

samples.summary: `renderReviewComment` mutates its caller's finding objects by writing `_lens` onto them.
samples.evidence: `for (const f of findings) f._lens = l.title || l.id || "lens";` (line 148) mutates the input array's objects rather than working on copies. Harmless for the CLI path (objects come from a fresh JSON.parse), but any caller that renders twice with different lens titles, or reuses the same finding objects for another renderer, gets a stale/incorrect lens tag.

samples.summary: The 5k reserve assumed by `DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS = 60000` is not bounded by anything the workflow appends, so the backstop truncation can still produce a body over GitHub's 65536 limit.
samples.evidence: Line 27-29 reserves ~5k for marker + tally + `promptSection` + note, but `ai-prompt.mjs::renderAiPromptSection` emits one line per blocking finding with no cap, so `promptSection` can exceed 5k. The workflow's backstop (agent-review-on-demand.yml:600) then produces `slice(0, 64900) + note + tally + promptSection + note`, i.e. a body LONGER than 64900 + promptSection — potentially over 65536, which fails `issues.updateComment` and strands the placeholder. Pre-existing arithmetic, but this change is what introduces the 60000 assumption that it is safe.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. In the evidence-rebuild branch, `used` is seeded to preamble+heading (review-comment.mjs:256) and the evidence admission test (`used + head.length + evid.length <= budget`, :260) reserves no space for the heads of the remaining `shown` findings; the else branch (:263) appends those heads unconditionally with no budget check. Since the first pass only guarantees P+H+S <= budget, an early finding's evidence may consume up to budget−P−H−head0, after which the remaining heads still get appended, pushing the region up to ~2*budget — violating the module's own stated invariant at :229 ('enforcing it over EVERYTHING') and the never-drop-a-blocking-one-liner contract at :83-84/:230-234. Existing tests do not cover this shape: review-comment.test.mjs:162-171 uses 5000-char evidence against maxChars 1200, so no evidence ever passes the :260 test and the rebuild degenerates to head-only; :173-178 has no evidence at all. The only downstream protection is the blunt `body.slice(0, 64900)` in agent-review-on-demand.yml:600, which prevents a 422 but cuts mid-<details>/mid-fold and can remove blocking one-liners — a symptom mitigation, not a guard making the defect unreachable, so `already-guarded` does not apply. This is a boundary/accounting logic bug in the correctness lane with real truncation/data-presentation-loss impact.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: review-comment.mjs:168-170 contains exactly `l.gating !== false && l.applicable !== false && l.conclusion && l.conclusion !== "success"`, and the added truthiness clause makes a falsy conclusion render the 🟢 "looks good" header. The old inline computation it replaces (agent-review-on-demand.yml:543-544) did `const conclusion = p ? p.conclusion : 'failure'; if (blocking && applicable && conclusion !== 'success') blocked = true;`, which treated an undefined conclusion as blocked — so the safety direction really did flip from fail-closed to fail-open, contradicting the code comment at review-comment.mjs:166-167 that claims it is the "Same decision". collectLenses (line 313) `p.conclusion ?? (v ? v.conclusion : "failure")` only falls back to "failure" when verdict.json is missing/unparseable, so a parseable verdict.json (or panel entry) without a `conclusion` field yields undefined and prints 🟢 immediately above the populated "#### 🚫 Blocking (N)" section emitted at line 243. I checked the mitigating direction: the production writers (review-panel.mjs:2805/2808 writeVerdict, and all panelEntry call sites at 2209-2210, 2296-2297, 2578-2579) always set a non-empty conclusion, so the trigger needs malformed/foreign artifacts — but that is an incidental data property, not a guard: collectLenses is explicitly documented fail-safe over malformed files (lines 293-295) and renderReviewComment is exported and callable with arbitrary lens objects, so I cannot cite a check that makes the branch unreachable. Inverted condition on a verdict signal is squarely in the correctness lane, so no refutation ground applies.
